topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by linking concepts from histopathology practicals to the day's learning outcomes on cancer genetics and transformation.

topics.label: Tumor Viruses and Cellular Transformation Assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how the historical study of tumor-causing viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays for measuring cellular transformation.

topics.label: Oncogenes, Tumor Suppressor Genes, and Mutation Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define oncogenic versus tumor suppressor mutations, their functional effects on cell cycle checkpoint control, and their genetic mechanisms of action.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Forms of Genetic Instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how failures in distinct DNA repair pathways, replication machinery, and mitotic chromosome segregation generate sequence and chromosomal instability.

topics.label: Multistep Tumorigenesis and Hereditary Cancer Predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the stepwise model of mutation accumulation in tumor development and how inherited germline mutations accelerate cancer progression.

topics.label: Conclusion and Recommended Reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by reviewing the learning outcomes, suggesting supplementary reading, and previewing the next session.
